text.p: Biogen Inc said on Thursday it was "disappointed" with Britain's House of Lords ruling dismissing a hepatitis B treatment patent, but said it would continue to earn royalties in Britain from a separate patent.

"Although we expect to continue receiving our U.K. royalties of less than a million dollars annually based on the surviving hepatitis B patent, we are clearly disappointed by today's decision," Biogen chief executive Jim Vincent said.
Earlier British drug company Medeva Plc said the House of Lords dismissed Biogen's UK patent challenge to Medeva's hepatitis B treatment Hepagene.
In a statement, Vincent said the dismissed hepatitis B antigen patent had been "repeatedly" upheld by the European Patent Office, despite challenges by other companies.
"As a result, we are confident that this ruling will not affect the validity of our hepatitis B patent portfolio in other European countries or anywhere else in the world," he said.
The House of Lords ruling cannot be appealed.
Cambridge Mass-based Biogen's shares were off 3-1/4 at 75 in late morning after dropping 2-5/16 on Wednesday.
Lehman Brothers analyst Tony Butler said he did not think the British patent issue was a major event for Biogen and saw it having a "marginal effect" on its stock.

He linked recent weakness in the shares to profit taking amid investor concern that sales of its flagship product, the mutliple sclerosis treatment Avonex, might be slowing. But he said he did not think any slowdown showing in weekly Avonex sales data was a long-term trend.
"Avonex sales will continue to move higher," he said.
